skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
skills.reason: The opening warning at T2 stated the Committee and company are the client, not the witness, and that counsel cannot advise him personally.

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.
skills.reason: T2 said the privilege belongs to the company, which may waive it and disclose to government without consent; T4 checked understanding.

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.
skills.reason: T6 sets out the process, asks for complete answers, tells the witness to flag speculation, and asks them to say whether they remember or are reconstructing.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.
skills.reason: T4 asked the witness to state who was represented and who controls privilege, and T6 asked whether the plan was acceptable.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.
skills.reason: T374 covers confidentiality, keeping documents, not speaking with other witnesses and possible follow-up, and asks if anything needs adding; a clear next-steps or 'nothing else' sequence is thin.

moments.text: To be clear, we represent the Committee and the company only. We do not represent you personally, we are not your attorney, and we can't give you legal advice.
Explains the privilege belongs to the company, the company may disclose without consent, asks for openness and asks if he understands.
Before we go on, could you tell me in your own words your understanding of who we represent, and who controls the privilege?

Explains how the interview will run, asks for complete answers, flags speculation, asks him to say when he is reconstructing, and notes he may consult his own lawyer.
Closes with a reminder to keep documents and notes, keep the interview confidential, not discuss with witnesses, and says there may be follow-up.

skills.name: Narrative Development
skills.description: Lets the witness walk through what happened.
skills.reason: Open invitations at T16, T44, T80 and T310 let the witness walk through each topic before specifics.

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.
skills.reason: Questions generally moved from general to specific, but some topics such as Raptor returns and controls were jumped to quickly.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.
skills.reason: Most questions were clear, though some were compound, such as T340 combining family and Enron funding.

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.
skills.reason: Questions stayed polite and neutral throughout, and the interviewer kept control when the witness deflected, as at T306 and T332.

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.
